source_text: Examples of schemes, algebraic spaces, algebraic stacks

<STRUCT_0001>
The Stacks project currently contains two chapters discussing
moduli stacks and their properties, see
Moduli Stacks, Section <REF_0001> and
Moduli of Curves, Section <REF_0002>.
Over time we intend to add more, for example:
<STRUCT_0002>
<STRUCT_0003> <MATH_0001>,
i.e., principally polarized abelian schemes of genus <MATH_0002>,
<STRUCT_0004> <MATH_0003>, i.e.,
<MATH_0004>-pointed smooth projective genus <MATH_0005> curves,
<STRUCT_0005> <MATH_0006>, i.e., smooth projective genus <MATH_0007>-curves
with <MATH_0008> pairwise distinct labeled points,
<STRUCT_0006> <MATH_0009>, i.e.,
stable <MATH_0010>-pointed nodal projective genus <MATH_0011>-curves,
<STRUCT_0007> <MATH_0012>, moduli of morphisms
(with suitable conditions on the stacks <MATH_0013>, <MATH_0014>
and the base scheme <MATH_0015>),
<STRUCT_0008> <MATH_0016>, the stack of <MATH_0017>-bundles
of the geometric Langlands programme (with suitable conditions on the scheme
<MATH_0018>, the group scheme <MATH_0019>, and the base scheme <MATH_0020>),
<STRUCT_0009> <MATH_0021>, i.e., the Picard stack associated
to an algebraic stack over a base scheme (or space).
<STRUCT_0010>
More generally, the Stacks project is somewhat
lacking in geometrically meaningful examples.
